cards.name: Snorlax
cards.whyItBelongs: This Snorlax was drawn by a fan: Keita Takahashi’s entry won CoroCoro’s Pokémon illustration contest in 1998 and was printed as a real card. Snorlax has dozed off sitting in the middle of the road, eyes shut, exactly as its Pokédex entry warns it might, and its Guard power means nobody gets past. Its own attack even puts it back to sleep.

cards.name: Snorlax
cards.whyItBelongs: Out cold with comic-strip Z's. A holy-grail vintage promo that defined what it means to be the Sleeping Pokémon.

cards.name: Rocket's Snorlax
cards.whyItBelongs: Snorlax is flat on its belly on a dusty floor, completely out, with its face smooshed to the ground and a faint smile on its lips. The ground around it is a snack-and-litter aftermath: an empty soda bottle, a crushed can, a cup, scattered wrappers, a bit of discarded junk. It looks like Snorlax ate everything in reach, made a mess, and collapsed on the spot without bothering to clean up. This is probably the most committed sleeper in the whole stack.

cards.name: Snorlax
cards.whyItBelongs: Snorlax is relaxing in a hot spring with only its big face above the surface, and steam curls up around it from the warm water. Far off in the distance, snowy mountains fade into the haze. Its eyes are shut in two flat lines, its small fangs show, and its expression says it has no plans to leave. The scenery is cool and quiet, but Snorlax is clearly the one who found the warmest spot around.

cards.name: Snorlax
cards.whyItBelongs: Snorlax is flopped face-down in a woodland clearing, sunk into a bed of white flowers, with leaves drifting past and sunlight coming through the trees. Its eyes are closed, there’s a small satisfied smile on its face, and its big round body is draped over the grass like a giant, very soft boulder. It’s one of the most gently peaceful pieces of art in the stack.

cards.name: Snorlax
cards.whyItBelongs: Snorlax is sprawled across an open field of tall green grass. There’s no scenery to compete with it, no trees, flowers or water, just Snorlax and a lot of soft grass, which makes it the most stripped-down, purely lazy sleeper in sleeping Snorlax set. It looks like it dropped where it stood and fell asleep right there.

cards.name: Snorlax
cards.whyItBelongs:
Snorlax is rolling through a sunlit town fast asleep, curled into a huge round ball with its eyes shut and a dust cloud trailing behind it. A crowd of startled townspeople is scattering out of the way, with one man mid-leap and a couple of others looking alarmed, while on the right a woman seems to be calmly holding up her phone to take a photo. This is a very different kind of nap from the rest of the Snorlax cards: it’s the only one causing a stampede. The painted, slightly storybook style makes it funnier, since everyone is panicking over an unstoppable sleeper.

The card is all about this scene. Toss and Turn can be used even while Snorlax is Asleep, and if it is, the attack does 90 more damage. That’s the sleep-rolling you see in the artwork, where being asleep is what makes it so dangerous.

cards.name: Snorlax
cards.whyItBelongs: A full-on Snorlax nap under the trees, with two Pikachu nearby and a Torchic perched on his head. Nobody in this scene looks in a hurry to wake him.

cards.name: Snorlax
cards.whyItBelongs: Snorlax is sprawled on the ground beneath a tree, arms and legs flung wide and mouth open mid-snore. The view looks down through leafy branches, so the leaves frame the scene and the branches throw dappled shadows across its big round belly. The green light and the cool shade make it look like the perfect spot for an afternoon sleep.

cards.name: Snorlax
cards.whyItBelongs: A soft night sky, a cozy patch of ground, and Snorlax sleeping through it all. A classic little bedtime scene.

cards.name: Snorlax
cards.whyItBelongs: Out cold slumped against a forest tree. Atsuko Nishida's warm, storybook illustration of Snorlax in heavy slumber after a feast.

cards.name: Snorlax
cards.whyItBelongs: Food coma flat on its back under an apple tree. Oswaldo KATO captures Snorlax completely dead to the world, surrounded by half-eaten apples with bite marks.

cards.name: Snorlax
cards.whyItBelongs: Out cold blocking a real-world entrance. The classic Pokémon GO encounter where Snorlax makes public concrete steps its personal bed.

cards.name: Snorlax
cards.whyItBelongs: Out cold in a field of yellow flowers. Pure pastoral bliss for the original heavy sleeper resting its heavy chin on its arm.

cards.name: Snorlax
cards.whyItBelongs: Cozy nap on a flowery hill. Handcrafted in amigurumi yarn by Asako Ito, Snorlax lets out a big sleepy yawn amidst tiny pastel felt flowers.

cards.name: Snorlax
cards.whyItBelongs: Snorlax has simply fallen asleep wherever it pleased, sprawled beside a quiet pond while the park carries on around it. A Pidgey has turned its enormous belly into a perch and a Diglett pops up from the path nearby, neither doing anything to disturb the nap. GOSSAN turns Snorlax’s legendary ability to sleep through absolutely everything into its own tiny ecosystem.

cards.name: Snorlax
cards.whyItBelongs: Food coma among wild forest berries and mushrooms. Aya Kusube’s richly textured fairytale style shows Snorlax completely knocked out digesting a woodland feast.

cards.name: Chansey
cards.whyItBelongs: Chansey bustles through the bright Pokemon Center while Snorlax has simply nodded off on the tiled floor. The room carries on around it, making that unbothered floor nap the perfect cozy sleeper cameo.
